blogs.title: Triple Threat: Navigating the Anatomical Minefield of TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV
blogs.description: This post examines the escalating technical complexity of performing a third transcatheter aortic valve implantation in a patient with two prior TAV prostheses. With expanding TAVI indications and improving survival, clinicians will increasingly encounter patients with multiple overlapping valve frames. We discuss the challenges of frame layering, stent mesh burden, valve selection in narrow anatomies, and the current evidence base for serial transcatheter reinterventions—which remains remarkably sparse. The post focuses on the procedural strategy itself, including the rationale for selecting a self-expanding Acurate neo2 prosthesis with supra-annular leaflets and low frame height, balloon pre- and post-dilation technique, and how high-pressure post-dilation may have contributed to partial mechanical expansion of the prior Evolut frame.

blogs.title: TAVI After Treated Prosthetic Endocarditis: Where Do Guidelines End and Clinical Judgment Begin?
blogs.description: This post explores the clinical tension between the 2025 ESC guidelines recommending surgical valve replacement for prosthetic valve endocarditis and the reality of patients with prohibitive surgical risk who have no viable surgical option. Using this case as a springboard, we discuss how the decision to proceed with transcatheter reintervention was made only after documented infection resolution (negative blood cultures, TEE confirmation, CT imaging), and how management aligned with non-endocarditis cases once active infection was excluded. We review the evidence for transcatheter approaches in post-PVE patients, the role of multidisciplinary heart team decision-making, and the ethical and clinical considerations of offering a third TAVI in a patient where future options are effectively exhausted.

blogs.title: Preserving Coronary Access Across Three Valve Frames: The Role of CT-Guided Neo-Skirt Planning
blogs.description: This post focuses on the critical role of preprocedural multislice CT in planning complex TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV procedures, with particular emphasis on coronary artery obstruction risk and future coronary access preservation. We discuss the concept of the 'neo-skirt' formed by the pinned leaflets of prior transcatheter valves, how valve-to-coronary distance measurements informed the decision to implant high within the Evolut frame without coronary protection, and how commissural alignment was planned using CT modelling and fluoroscopic landmarks. The post also addresses the limitations of current CT assessment techniques (absence of dedicated 3D expansion analysis software) and why coronary obstruction risk escalates with each successive valve-in-valve procedure.

blogs.title: The 67 mmHg to 26 mmHg Journey: Understanding Early Gradients and PPM After Triple Valve Implantation
blogs.description: This post analyzes the striking hemodynamic evolution observed after the third TAVI—an immediate post-procedural mean gradient of 67 mmHg consistent with severe prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM), which improved dramatically to 26 mmHg at 1 month and remained stable at 1 year. We explore the mechanisms behind this phenomenon, including delayed self-expansion of the Acurate neo2 frame, the contribution of commissural alignment, high-pressure balloon post-dilation effects on the prior Evolut frame, and left ventricular remodeling. The post discusses the clinical implications of accepting a high early gradient in multi-valve configurations, how to counsel patients and families about expected improvement, and what parameters should prompt concern rather than watchful waiting.

blogs.title: Planning for the Third Valve at the Time of the First: Lifetime Management of Structural Valve Disease
blogs.description: This post steps back from the procedural details to address the broader paradigm shift toward lifetime management planning in structural valve disease. Using this patient's 10-year journey from a Lotus valve in 2014 through endocarditis and two subsequent interventions, we discuss how the initial valve choice (a mechanically retractable Lotus valve) influenced downstream options, why commissural alignment at the first intervention matters for all future procedures, and how the interventional cardiology community should be thinking about TAVI trajectories in younger and lower-risk patients. We also discuss emerging rescue technologies such as BASILICA and bioprosthetic valve fracture, and the sobering reality that in triple-stented configurations, these bail-out options remain largely untested.
